title: Introduce sparse-metadata inference + heuristic compatibility layer and release-note synth
author: Elena Park
release_notes: Auto-infer missing model metadata (tokenizer, context_window, dtype) when onboarding sparse manifests.
Introduce a heuristic compatibility layer that suggests fallback model variants and quantization profiles for serving/resilience.
Generate concise release-note snippets from profile diffs to automate changelog creation.
description:
Motivation: many incoming model manifests during onboarding are sparse (missing tokenizer, context_window, or quantization hints). This causes manual back-and-forth, slows rollouts, and leads to inconsistent performance profiles in the registry. This PR adds two complementary features: 1) an inference pass that derives best-effort metadata from artifacts and lightweight probing; 2) a heuristic compatibility layer that scores and recommends fallback variants (smaller context, quantized variants, or compatible back-compat model family) and emits a compact release-note snippet summarizing the inferred changes for changelogs.

What this changes (high level):
- New inference module: src/onboard/infer_metadata.py. Runs during CLI/HTTP onboarding if manifest is missing fields; performs tokenizer detection (by byte-pattern + small sample tokenization), context window estimation from model config and param count heuristics, and dtype/quantization suggestions via probe-run with short input. Inferred values are persisted under the model version as `inferred_metadata` and flagged in UI/CLI.
- Compatibility layer: src/onboard/compat_layer.py. Computes a compatibility score across known variants (fp16, int8/ggml, reduced-context variants). Provides ranked recommendations used by onboarding UX and the release-note synthesizer. Intended to be conservative (prefers recommend-not-enforce).
- Release-note synthesizer: tooling that converts profile diffs and the inferred_metadata delta into a concise 1-3 line changelog snippet. Hook added to the release draft pipeline to auto-populate candidate notes for reviewers. Implemented in src/onboard/changelog_synth.py and wired into the assemble pipeline.
- CLI flag: --force-infer / --no-infer to opt into/out of inference pass. Default is on for self-serve flows and off for enterprise-private installs (explicit opt-in via config).
- DB migration: scripts/migrate_add_inferred_metadata.sql adds a nullable jsonb column `inferred_metadata` to model_versions table, with an inexpensive backfill for recent uploads.
- Tests + docs: tests for heuristic scoring and tokenizer detection (tests/test_infer_metadata.py), plus updated onboarding docs (docs/onboarding.md) and an example showing how to opt-out.

Why this approach: automated inference reduces manual triage for >50% of incoming model manifests we saw in the last quarter; the compatibility layer improves rollout resilience by recommending safe fallback variants rather than causing silent mismatches at serving time. The changelog snippet automation reduces author friction when releasing slight-profile-only changes.

Security & correctness notes: the inference pass is read-only against model artifacts and does not execute arbitrary model code; the short probing run uses a sandboxed runtime with a 2-token sample and strict CPU/GPU timeouts. All inferred metadata is explicitly marked as inferred and surfaced for human approval before it is used for automated rollouts.

Checklist:
- [x] inference engine and compatibility scoring implemented
- [x] DB migration and backfill script added
- [x] CLI wiring and opt-out flags
- [x] unit tests covering tokenizer detection and scoring heuristics
- [x] docs and changelog synth examples
- [x] QA: manual sample set verification (100 models)

Follow-ups (roadmap):
- Add telemetry to measure inference accuracy and false-positive rate (ENG-2210 follow-up).
- Add a compact human-review UI to accept/reject inferred metadata during onboarding.

Related work: reuses tokenization heuristics from the eval-harness token-utils module and compatibility scoring design from earlier perf-canary work. Links: Linear ENG-2012, ENG-2210.

Summary: Adds pragmatic, opt-out inference for sparse manifests, a conservative compatibility layer for recommending fallbacks, and automated short release-note drafting for profile-only changes. This should reduce onboarding friction and improve release hygiene for incremental model updates.
